class.name: FellowRain3D
class.brief_description: Rain around the camera and wet surfaces where it falls: darker, glossier materials and puddles with ripples (FellowEngine).
class.description: Drops fall in a box of [member area] around the current camera (GPU particles: lit streaks along their velocity, [member wind] included, facing the camera), stop where they hit the scene as seen from above and splash there ([member splashes]). While the node is active, the Forward+ renderer wets every opaque material after the material's own code ([code]fragment()[/code] of a [ShaderMaterial] too), in the depth pre-pass as well as the colour pass so screen-space and other reflections see the result: by [member wetness], porous surfaces (rough, not metallic) darken, all of them get a glossy film, and on flat rough ground puddles form ([member puddles]): flat, smooth standing water with the rain's ripples ([member ripple_tile], [member ripple_strength]). Undersides and surfaces under a roof stay dry: the scene's top seen from above (a [GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D] of [member occlusion_size] following the camera, the drops' collider) tells where the rain reaches. A [FellowWater3D] shows the ripples on its surface too. Transparent materials are not wetted. With [member precipitation] [constant PRECIPITATION_SNOW] it snows instead, and [member snow] covers what faces up with snow where it falls (decision record [code]docs/decisions/0128-snow.md[/code]). One node at a time is active: the last one to enter the tree. Wetness can follow the rain over time ([member wetness_follows_rain]). [code]rendering/fellow/fluid/enabled[/code] off turns the wetting off. The drops and the heightfield are internal children ([method get_drops], [method get_occlusion]). Decision record [code]docs/decisions/0124-rain.md[/code]. In the editor the drops fall, and the ripples and wetting move, only while it updates continuously (Editor Settings > Interface > Editor > Update Continuously); by default the editor redraws only when something changes, and shows the wet, snowy scene still (milestone 52).

method.name: get_drops
method.description: The internal particles of the drops (their sub-emitter makes the splashes).

method.name: get_occlusion
method.description: The internal heightfield of the scene seen from above: the drops collide with it and surfaces below its top stay dry. Its [member GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.heightfield_mask] picks the layers that shelter.

method.name: get_rain_here
method.description: The share of [member rain] falling at the camera under [member showers] (1 without them).

method.name: get_ripple_texture
method.description: The rain's ripples on standing water: a tiling texture of [member ripple_tile] (slopes in red and green, height in blue, the puddles' tiling noise in alpha; with mipmaps), computed every frame while the node is active.

method.name: stamp
method.description: Presses a capsule from [param from] to [param to] (their x and z) of [param radius] into the snow, [param depth] metres deep (negative: 0.8 of [member snow_depth]), once — a footprint, a groove. Applied in the next frames, within the tracks' window around the camera.

members.member: The side of the box around the camera the drops fall in, in metres.

The colour of the drops and splashes; alpha is their opacity at the middle of a streak. They are lit by the sky's ambient and the scene's lights (brighter with a light behind them), so the rain is dark at night but where lights shine through it.
A drop's streak in metres: width and length (the path a frame's exposure sees). Drops within 0.5 m of the camera are not drawn; they fade in to 4 m.
The falling speed of the drops, in metres per second (the terminal speed of a raindrop of a few millimetres).

Between dry and wet (0 < [member wetness] < 1) the surfaces are wet in patches — the high spots drying first and wetting last — and the puddles shrink to their deepest instead of fading (0-1; 0: an even wetness, the puddles fading). At [member wetness] 0 and 1 it changes nothing.
With [member wetness_follows_rain], the seconds a fully wet scene takes to dry once the rain stops.
The height above the camera the drops start from, in metres.
The snowflakes' colour and opacity (with [member precipitation] [constant PRECIPITATION_SNOW]).
How far, in metres, a snowflake swings about its path as it falls, at a rate of its own.
The snowflakes' diameter in metres (each flake 0.5 to 1.5 times it).
How fast the snowflakes fall, in metres per second.

How fast, per second, the snowflakes take the wind where they are, gusts included, when the scene has a [FellowWind3D] and [member wind_from_scene] is on (the Wind group of [ParticleProcessMaterial]).

How much of the water on the ground is ice (0-1): the puddles do not ripple, frozen glossy and a little milky, white at their thin edges; the wet film's gloss stays (glaze). A [FellowWeather3D] sets it from its temperature.
The seconds the water on the ground takes to freeze at 5 degrees below zero, and the hoarfrost to form under a clear sky, under a [FellowWeather3D] (which sets [member freeze] and [member frost]).

Hoarfrost (0-1): white, rough, glinting crystals on what faces the sky where the rain would reach (less on walls, none underneath), in a feathery pattern that spreads as it grows. A [FellowWeather3D] grows it below freezing when nothing falls, slower under clouds.
The number of drops at full [member rain]; [member rain] scales the number drawn.
With [member snow_follows_precipitation], the seconds a full [member snow] cover takes to melt while it does not snow.
If [code]true[/code], the heightfield of the scene seen from above is rendered again every frame (for moving roofs: vehicles, doors); otherwise when it moves with the camera.
The height of the heightfield's box, in metres, centred on the node's height.
The resolution of the heightfield (256 to 4096 texels a side). With the default [member occlusion_size], 1024 is 8 cm a texel.
The side of the heightfield around the camera, in metres. Beyond it everything is exposed to the rain.

Rain, or snow: flakes drifting down around the camera instead of drops (they live in a box around it, follow the scene's wind and swing as they fall), and no ripples or splashes. The surfaces are covered with snow by [member snow], whatever falls.
How much of flat, rough ground is covered by puddles once it is wet (0: none, 1: nearly all).
How hard it rains (0 to 1): the number of drops, the ripples on standing water and, with [member wetness_follows_rain], how fast surfaces get wet.

The rainbow's strength (0: none). While it rains, or lately rained (the rain seen fades over 90 s once it stops: the rain moving away), and the sun shines on it, the primary and secondary bows appear around the point opposite the sun, over the sky and over what stands far enough behind the rain. The clouds' shadow at the camera, or a [FellowWeather3D]'s sunlight, dims them. Decision record [code]docs/decisions/0134-rainbows.md[/code].
A scale of the ripples' slopes on puddles and on wet flat ground.
The size in metres of the tile of the ripple texture (two offset lookups hide the repeat).

The strength of the rain shafts under the volumetric clouds (0: none): while it rains (or snows), grey curtains hang below the clouds' dense parts in the distance (from 2 km on), streaked along the fall and drifting with the clouds. Needs [code]rendering/fellow/post/clouds/enabled[/code]. Decision record [code]docs/decisions/0135-rain-shafts.md[/code].

Showers (0-1): with the volumetric clouds on, it rains at the camera only as the clouds above let it — where their layer is dense (the rain shafts' share: none below 0.7 of their local coverage, all of it from 0.95), eased over 2 s as showers pass with the clouds' wind. The drops, the ripples, the wetting and the snow's settling follow it; the rain shafts and the rainbow keep the [member rain] set. At 0 it rains everywhere as set; without the clouds too. See [method get_rain_here].

How much the [member snow] cover is soaked with its meltwater (0-1): greyer, glossier, without glints, its thin parts first. A [FellowWeather3D] sets it while the snow melts (fully at 3 °C and above, or in the rain).

The snow cover, from 0 to 1: what faces up is covered where the snow falls (not under roofs: the heightfield of [method get_occlusion]) — patchy while thin, everything facing up once deep, nothing on slopes steeper than 60 degrees. Fresh snow: white, rough, smooth (it fills the materials' relief) with gentle undulations, glinting by [member snow_sparkle]. Opaque materials on the Forward+ renderer, in the depth pre-pass and the colour pass, after their own code.
How deep the snow is, in metres: tracks that reach it show the ground ([FellowSnowTracker3D], [method stamp]).
If [code]true[/code], [member snow] grows while it snows (fully in [member snowing_time] at [member rain] 1) and melts otherwise (in [member melting_time]).
The glints of fresh snow, from 0 to 1: crystals in cells of 8 mm, one in 20 turned at random, shining where one faces the light; faded where a cell is smaller than a pixel.
With [member snow_follows_precipitation], the seconds full snowfall takes to cover the ground.
If [code]true[/code], drops splash where they land (two small droplets each, a sub-emitter at collision, fading over 0.3 s).

Thin streaks (m; 0: off): the drops' own width. A streak is drawn at this width or a pixel at its distance, whichever is wider, its opacity scaled by their ratio — thin and faint in the distance, as rain is seen, instead of bars of [member drop_size]'s width at every distance (which read heavy in daylight, against the sun). 0.004 is a large drop's streak.
The ripples' and showers' clock in seconds (not saved): advanced by the process time with [member time_auto], or set here for deterministic renders.
If [code]true[/code], the ripples' time advances with the process time; otherwise it is set by the [member time] property (deterministic renders).
The seconds full snowfall ([member rain] 1) takes to fill a track of [member snow_depth] back (0: never).
The tracks' texture side in cells (a power of two; R16F).
The side of the tracks' window around the camera, in metres (48 m at 2048 cells: 2.3 cm each).

If [code]true[/code], the snow keeps tracks: [FellowSnowTracker3D]s and [method stamp] press them in, the cover shows them (their walls, packed snow at their bottom, the ground where they reach [member snow_depth], a rim beside them), and the falling snow fills them back ([member track_refill_time]). They live in a window of [member track_window] around the camera, anchored to the world: a place that leaves the window is fresh snow when it comes back.
How wet surfaces exposed to the rain are (0 to 1). Puddles appear above 0.4.
If [code]true[/code], [member wetness] grows while it rains (in [member wetting_time] at full rain) and falls when it does not (in [member drying_time]).
With [member wetness_follows_rain], the seconds full rain takes to make a dry scene fully wet.

The wind carrying the drops, in metres per second: their streaks lean with it and they start upwind of the camera so they land around it. With [member wind_from_scene] and a [FellowWind3D] in the scene, that node's wind is used instead.

Wind-driven rain (0-1): in a wind the drops fall slanted, and the shelter follows them — a surface is wet where the slanted path from it up into the rain is open, so walls facing the wind get wet under their eaves (and as wet as the ground) while the lee of a building stays drier. From a drift of 0.2 m per metre of fall (a breeze of 1.8 m/s at the default [member drop_speed]: the rain as good as vertical, nothing changes) to fully slanted at 0.6. Not for snow.
If [code]true[/code] and the scene has a [FellowWind3D], the drops are carried by its wind at the camera (with the gust there) instead of [member wind].

constants.constant: Drops: lit streaks falling from above the camera, splashing where they land.
Snowflakes: soft discs drifting down around the camera, swinging as they fall and following the scene's wind.
